{{Top|leg}}
'''Yaam Sector''' or '''Sector 1Y4F''', the lower levels of which were known as the '''Blackpit Slums''', was a district on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the early years of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Twilight">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref>

Yaam Sector was one of the oldest-established urban districts on Coruscant, but it had become peripheral to the planet's cityscape, located about five thousand kilometers west of central areas such as [[Zi-Kree Sector]], and around four hundred kilometers to the north, placing it outside the densest belt of skytowers around Coruscant's equator, and away from the main [[hypertube]] [[Hovertrain/Legends|mag-lev]] system. Visitors traveling to Yaam Sector by mass transit had to leave the high-speed hypertube at [[Ts'chai Station]], and take a slower monorail connection northwards to [[Yaam Depot]], though it was also possible to make a direct journey by [[speeder bus]].<ref name="Twilight" />

The region was similarly distant from the [[Southern Underground/Legends|Southern Underground]].<ref name="Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref>

Yaam Sector covered nearly eighty square kilometers, and principally consisted of [[Skyscraper|cloudcutters]], skyscrapers which topped out between 700 and 800 meters, with only a small number of the taller 1&ndash;2 km skytowers that were common in the equatorial belt. The towers were particularly close together, a result of the sector retaining its ancient layout of narrow groundways, which formed a claustrophobic maze of irregular streets, pedestrian alleys and dead ends between the ancient bases of the towering buildings.<ref name="Twilight" />

While the upper levels of Yaam Sector's cloudcutters were relatively salubrious, the dingy lower levels formed a notorious area known as the Blackpit Slums. The demarcation was given physical form, as the upper air was kept clear by [[Air scrubber/Legends|air scrubber]] droids, but beneath the altitudes at which they worked, a permanent layer of smog around Level 155 was created by a combination of the smoky fires which slum-dwellers lit for warmth, and emissions from the generators which they used for power.<ref name="Twilight" />

Beneath the smog, the larger landmarks were often industrial&mdash;a mix of factories, warehouses, docking bays, power stations, and waste-disposal infrastructure. Machines known as [[wallcrawlers]] used vertical tracks on the sides of buildings to haul cargo to higher levels.<ref name="Twilight" />

With limited [[airspeeder]] traffic, much of the slums' sentient activity took place at street level. Here the permanent twilight was illuminated by a random variety of different street-light technologies and a vast number of holographic advertising displays, some of them offering blatantly illegal products and services. The groundways carried a mix of street food, multi-species foot traffic, [[rickshaw]] droids, single-seat [[Weaver (speeder)|weavers]] and conventional ground skimmers, though in some areas these traveled at an altitude of about ten meters above the busy streets, and there were pedestrian balconies a similar height off the ground, accessed by [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] [[Turbolift/Legends|drop-tubes]].<ref name="Twilight" />

Typical of the street-level slums were hostels known as [[resicube]]s or [[resiblock]]s, sturdy [[ferrocrete]] structures containing windowless, cell-like rooms. One such building was the [[Coruscant Arms]], thirty meters tall and located on a pedestrian alley known as [[Amator Avenue]], where [[Jax Pavan]] had a [[micro-conapt]] measuring two meters by three, set against a solid exterior wall some ten centimeters thick. The cell which [[Den Dhur]] rented by the night while searching for Pavan was even smaller&mdash;a cramped cube barely two meters square within walls fifteen meters thick, equipped with a single bed, chair and table, which all formed part of the ferrocrete structure, with minimal furnishing such as the [[Foamcast/Legends|foamcast]] mattress for the bed, plus alcoves for a food unit and a primitive water-shower [[Refresher/Legends|refresher]].<ref name="Twilight" />

One ground-level location in the Blackpit Slums, [[Tangor Square]], had a wider reputation on Coruscant as an entertainment district, including numerous [[holoparlor]]s and a [[Shronker/Legends|shronker]] salon.<ref name="Twilight" /> 

The lower levels also extended to locations higher in the cloudcutters. [[Gort's]], located on Level 50, was a [[Mon Calamari]] restaurant serving good Quarren [[sulyet]] in its bar.<ref name="Twilight" />

Much of the lower city was effectively controlled by criminal groups, ranging from street gangs to [[Rokko]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]], who controlled the district's holoparlors in the early era of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], and resided in an underground palace fifty meters below surface level, decorated with ancient vistas of [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]] created by the Hutt artist [[Gorgo]].<ref name="Twilight" />

According to a computer search conducted by [[Haninum Tyk Rhinann]], in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] Yaam Sector was home to 8,675 [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|males]] named [[Jax Pavan (name)|Jax Pavan]], one of them the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]].<ref name="Twilight" />

==Behind the scenes==
Yaam Sector is a major setting in ''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight|Jedi Twilight]]'', the first novel of the ''[[Coruscant Nights/Legends|Coruscant Nights]]'' trilogy.

The novel does not explicitly state Yaam Sector is west of uptown Galactic City, but implies it by mentioning its "earlier time zone" than the Zi-Kree Sector, and that the system's primary has "not yet set" when the body clocks of beings arriving from central districts expect the start of night.
